observation.visible_scene: A vertical column of falling liquid is filmed against a near-black background, surrounded by a fine spray of bright droplets. In the upper-right corner a soft, out-of-focus pinkish-tan form (consistent with a hand or limb) and a small orange blob at the right edge remain in roughly the same position throughout. The liquid stream occupies the center of the frame.
visible_changes: Early frames (t=0.00–0.44) show a thin, broken stream: the column is narrow, wavy, and interrupted by gaps, with a clumpy mid-section and scattered droplets above and to the right.

Mid frames (t=0.48–0.84) the column becomes visibly thicker and more continuous, a solid ribbon of liquid with internal reflective streaks and a wavy surface, while the surrounding droplet spray persists.
Later frames (t=0.88–1.00) the stream broadens into a dark sheet filling much of the center, suggesting the framing tightens on the column (zoom/approach) or the flow widens.

Final frames (t=1.04–1.60) the image goes dark and defocused; the liquid column is no longer sharply resolved, and a vertical multicolored patterned band (green/purple/pink swirls) appears left-of-center, with the pinkish top-right form still present.

The center-of-stream position drifts slightly to the right across the clip (from ~x=520 early to ~x=560 mid), and the overall view appears to move closer to the column rather than the column translating across the frame.
outside_clip_unknowns: What source or device produces the liquid stream and the spray.
The identity of the pinkish form and orange blob at the top right.
What the colorful patterned surface in the late frames is and whether it was always present but out of focus.
The moment the stream began and what happens after the excerpt ends.
uncertain_details: Whether the apparent thickening of the column is due to camera zoom/approach, a focus change, or an actual increase in flow rate.
Whether individual droplets are moving downward or are essentially static specks against the dark background.
Whether the colorful patterned band is a separate object revealed by refocusing or a background element seen through the liquid.
The exact cause of the loss of detail and darkening in the final frames (focus shift, exposure change, or occlusion).

Both ends are arbitrary crop boundaries, not the beginning and completion of an action. Motion
may already be underway in the first view and may continue beyond the last. The endpoints need
NOT match or connect as a loop. Do not judge different endpoints as a physical inconsistency,
and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.
Do not supply named physics laws. Compare each important entity's first and last image positions
and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
Return JSON {"visible_scene":"...", "visible_changes":["observation supported within the excerpt"],
"outside_clip_unknowns":["unseen prerequisites or outcomes, only when relevant"],
"uncertain_details":["..."]}. Be concrete and concise, in English. This is not a complete event reconstruction.
